  WHY: This bypasses the fenced-example stripping applied to other marker reads. A prompted command example inside a fenced block containing `**Occurrences:** 5` or similar can populate the verdict with arbitrary, untrusted data, violating the trust boundary the PR establishes.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:123 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The regex matches only fences opened by exactly four backticks followed by the literal `text\n`.
  WHY: Other fence styles (e.g., three backticks, different language specifiers like `bash`, or indented fences) bypass the stripping, leaving marker text inside them visible to the metadata parser and bypassing the intended trust boundary. While `issue_body()` currently writes four-backtick `text` fences, this is an incomplete implementation of the "strip quoted blocks first" principle for an untrusted input.
